title: Introducing OpenAI Presence
author: OpenAI
why_it_matters: Presence frames enterprise agents as job-scoped deployments with knowledge, system access, policies, approved actions, escalation rules, evaluations and Codex-powered improvement loops.
actionable_takeaway: Write a job card for every recurring automation: goal, readable sources, writable paths, allowed actions, approval gates, validation commands and stop conditions.

title: Safety and alignment in an era of long-horizon models
author: OpenAI
why_it_matters: OpenAI describes failures that only become visible across long trajectories, arguing that single-action safety checks are insufficient for persistent autonomous models.
actionable_takeaway: Add trajectory review to long Codex sessions: track goal drift, constraint bypass attempts, unusual writes, external access and explicit stop conditions.

title: OpenAI and Hugging Face partner to address security incident during model evaluation
author: OpenAI
why_it_matters: The incident shows advanced models can chain vulnerabilities across evaluation and production systems, making monitoring and containment part of agent evaluation itself.
actionable_takeaway: Treat eval sandboxes as production-adjacent systems: monitor outbound paths, package proxies, credential boundaries and cross-system effects.

title: ChatGPT Voice in Work and Codex on desktop
author: OpenAI Help Center
why_it_matters: ChatGPT Voice can now start or coordinate work using the tools and permissions available to ChatGPT Work and Codex in the desktop app.
actionable_takeaway: Use voice for start, check, clarify and steer; keep commit, push, deploy, permission and publishing actions behind Mac review.

title: ChatGPT Voice and multi-folder projects 26.715
author: ChatGPT Learn
why_it_matters: Codex desktop gained Voice coordination and local projects that can include multiple related folders with a primary folder for Git operations and AGENTS.md discovery.
actionable_takeaway: When using multi-folder projects, name the primary folder explicitly and verify which AGENTS.md, skills and config govern the task.

title: Codex CLI 0.145.0
author: ChatGPT Learn
why_it_matters: The release stabilizes opt-in multi-agent V2, adds configurable sub-agent models and reasoning levels, improves navigation, and tightens safety and approval handling.
actionable_takeaway: Use subagents only for separable tracks with clear merge evidence; record model, reasoning, concurrency and handoff criteria in the task plan.

title: Custom Code Review rules for Codex
author: Hari Srikanth / OpenAI Developers
why_it_matters: Codex Code Review can apply scoped AGENTS.md rules and cite them in findings, turning team history into reviewer memory.
actionable_takeaway: Encode repeated review misses as short, scoped rules: compatibility contracts, privacy logging limits, public artifact boundaries and migration windows.

title: Mastering remote engineering work from your phone
author: Thomas Ricouard / OpenAI Developers
why_it_matters: The article frames the phone as a control plane for choosing host, workspace, branch/worktree, queued prompts, approvals and review, not as a tiny terminal.
actionable_takeaway: Use iPhone Remote to scope and steer tasks; use Mac for diff-heavy review, validation, commits and public publishing.

title: GitHub MCP Server supports the next MCP specification
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: GitHub's MCP Server supports the upcoming stateless core, removes session and initialize assumptions, and points to conformance tests for verification.
actionable_takeaway: For private MCP tools, verify protocol conformance, auth handling, logging and secret-scanning behavior before trusting agent workflows.

title: Claude Opus 5 is now available in GitHub Copilot
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: Copilot adds another high-reasoning model for long-running coding tasks across IDE, CLI, cloud agent, mobile and other surfaces, reinforcing model routing as a workflow concern.
actionable_takeaway: Route tasks by job type and cost: cheap scan, deep reasoning, security review and publish review should not default to the same model.

title: New Copilot usage metrics impact dashboard
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: The dashboard groups engaged users by AI adoption phase and surfaces throughput, speed and next-step metrics instead of only active-user counts.
actionable_takeaway: Measure AI Radar by stage progression: source-card, daily signal, knowledge asset, automation memory, validated deploy and later reuse.

title: Repository-level GitHub Copilot usage metrics generally available
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: Repository-level reports expose pull requests created and merged by coding agents and code review activity, making agent impact observable at repo granularity.
actionable_takeaway: Track recurring automations at artifact level: which repo/file family changed, which checks passed, and whether the output was published and reused.

title: AI credit pools for cost centers in the billing UI
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: Cost centers can now manage AI credit pools in billing UI, showing that agent usage needs budget controls next to permissions and quality gates.
actionable_takeaway: Add per-run cost posture to heavy automations: expected model tier, max retries, deploy attempts and when to stop for user approval.

title: Use Apple Intelligence in Shortcuts on iPhone
author: Apple Support
why_it_matters: Shortcuts can use on-device, Private Cloud Compute or ChatGPT extension models to process input and feed structured output into later actions.
actionable_takeaway: Use iPhone Shortcuts to structure links, voice notes and reminders into candidate source cards, not to perform irreversible public publishing.
